items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: It was in December 1943 that I made records with the great Lester Young.

ctx.x: From Denver we went to the R.K.O. Orpheum Theater in Omaha, Nebraska. During the week, there was a dance which we went to after the last show. The name of the orchestra playing was called the Blue Devils, and one of the trumpet players I had met in Buffalo, New York, when I was there with the Scott band. His name was George Hutchinson.

He informed me that some of the orchestra were staying at the same place we were which was a very big rooming-house called the White House, because it was painted white. There was a room with a piano and one could buy bootleg whisky there. So we went to the White House after the dance which finished at 2 a.m. and started a jam session. The tenor sax in the Blue Devils band was a light-skinned, red-headed fellow and he told me his name was Lester Young.

Booker Pitman, Alfred Pratt and Leroy Hardy used to practice in between most of the shows and so did I. When the jam session was announced we were the only ones in the Cooper orchestra who sat in. I didn't remember any of the other musicians in the Blue Devils except George Hutchinson (whom I already knew) and Lester Young. I remember Lester because I had had so much enjoyment
